So General Abdel Razek ensured that the ABiH forces did stop it, but noted that the shelling from the SRK side continued. Again, the principle of proportionality. Even if it was counterbattery fire, it has to be proportionate. If it was retaliatory, there is no excuse. The next image is part of John Ashton -- one of John Ashton's maps. We see a section of the Marsal Tito Boulevard marked. He gave evidence that he observed some shelling along the boulevard between the 21st and 28th of September. There were five civilian casualties. They had been walking on the boulevard. Three were not seriously wounded; two were seriously wounded. There were more than 40 rounds fired during the incident. He gave evidence that he later learned that this was a technique of firing referred to as the iron cross. He was informed of that by a liaison officer for the Bosnian Serb authorities who were stationed in Germany. It was confirmed to him by Colonel Indic. It was confirmed again by a gunner who he met in Pale. The relevance of it to this trial is simply this: Firstly I make the observation it was impossible to detect on the ground, Ashton didn't. All that one would see would be multiple shells falling in an area. This was something which was important to those that fired the weapons. The pattern was in their heads, the cross. It didn't matter what the pattern was. The relevance of it is that it is a form of indiscriminate fire that shows a total depersonalisation of those who will suffer the consequences. For the sake only of maintaining a pattern in their heads, this part of the city was subjected to 40 rounds of shell fire. Next image, please. This is a photograph that he took of that incident. And I think, Mr. President, at this point, we need to move into private session, but just for a matter of less than a minute, if we could do that. So the images will stop, the voice will stop for about a minute in terms of outside --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to have a confirmation from the technical booth that during the next minute, until the moment that Mr. Ierace asks to go into open session again, that no picture will be visible even not indirect. Or do we close... Mr. Ierace, there is a risk that people in the public gallery could see something on our screens. So therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have an alternative suggestion. I won't show the image. It will just be voice. But first I have to see if we can skip past the image without it being seen. Yes, we can. So Mr. President, private session for a minute or so with no images.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll now turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Ierace. We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll go to the next image. And the relevant part of Dr. Radinovic's map for Cengic Vila and Nova Sarajevo now appears on the screen. I'm conscious of the time. I won't go through a lot of these symbols. A number are marked white as pre-indictment. Indeed, I think I'll leave it at that time. But if one checks also 149 and 129, they are also pre-indictment. They are to the right of the screen. 169, no detailed location was given for that, which was described as a brigade alternate firing position. No explanation as to why the number was placed there. Moving on, this was an Ashton map. The yellow arrow has been placed by the Prosecution on the map for the purposes of this address to better indicate position P3. Ashton said that that marks the place of the bakery which was constantly targeted. On one occasion, he saw a shell land close by and set a group of small shops ablaze. He said the fire then responded despite the fact the shells continued to come down. It very close to the UNHCR headquarters. UNPROFOR determined that the shelling came from Grbavica. Two photos were taken. We show one of these. Next image. And we see in the background what appear to be silos. Might I go into private session, Mr. President, for about 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll turn into private session for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We now see P4 on Ashton's map. In December of 1992, he was riding in an UNPROFOR vehicle and then saw someone wounded on the steps of a nearby building. At that point, a shell exploded near their vehicle. And we can go to the next image. We were coming from the angle you see on the photograph, he said. We stopped at that point. I got out, made the photograph, saw that there was someone wounded on the front step of the building. I ran over to assist after taking another photograph and found a dead woman between the two vehicles that were burning, but could not recover her. He said of the two people: "They were civilians. The man was an old man, and the woman was a young woman." Another issue raised by the Defence was whether women were legitimate military targets. There was evidence that there were female combatants, but that evidence was also that there were very few female combatants, and that the number of female combatants in the ABiH reduced dramatically after the first few months of the war. Therefore, to the extent that the Defence suggests that adult women could be considered prima facie to be combatants simply is not borne out by the evidence. And to the extent that such a submission suggests that even men of military age could be considered prima facie combatants when in civilian clothes is not supported by the law. To give a simple example, even in battle, an enemy advances together with medics and often with correspondents, with journalists. There are many who even at the front line are not combatants and are protected by international humanitarian law. Moving on to the next image, here we see the same map, P1, same area. Novo Sarajevo. The red arrow indicates a direction of fire. The green arrow indicates what we can faintly see to be the confrontation lines. The witness gave evidence that in April 1993, he got on a bus in front of the state hospital. It rounded a corner into an intersection where there had always been heavy sniping. Next image, please. It happened that he took this photograph of his fellow passengers on the bus. As they came into the intersection, a sniper fired into the bus. He said it was fired from a high angle going on its entry point and where it impacted inside the bus. He said there was a scream from one woman. But some people just stood there, even when the bullet came through. They didn't even bother to move. Next image. Thank you. We now see the same bus after the shot was fired. He said one gentleman who was on the bus standing next to me said to me afterwards before I left the scene, It doesn't matter if you duck, because the bullets go right through it anyway. The bus stop. Everyone got off quickly, ran for cover. He obtained the assistance of the UNHCR and UNPROFOR, they investigated and determined that the bullet came from above the sports stadium, territory which was held by the Bosnian Serb forces. The map shown earlier was marked by the witness to indicate the direction of fire. When one looks at the stadium position consistent with his evidence as to his source of fire, one must make an allowance. Next image, please. Here we have the sniping map for a number of incidents occurring in the region of Hrasno. There was a dispute as to the positions at the front line, the confrontation lines, to which I shall return at a later point. But at this stage, the evidence from the Prosecution was that the forward position of the SRK forces was along a ridge just beneath the ridge, thus affording a view of the city to the SRK who occupied the ridge. In other words, the confrontation lines were on the northern flank of the ridge running parallel and in the area of Osrenska Street. Although it was not put to any of the Prosecution witnesses who gave that evidence, the Defence in its case called a witness who said the contrary. That he was stationed there and the front line was on the southern flank of the ridge so that from SRK positions, they couldn't see the city. We'll now deal with incident 27. I'll come back to the issue of the front lines. Next image, please. Incident 27 was, as you will recall, the case of a 13-year-old boy who during a cease-fire wandered along this shop front area with his mother and sister. He and his sister indeed had been evacuated from Sarajevo because his schoolteacher father and his mother were concerned as to the safety of their children. But this was not in 1994; this was post Markale. This was when there was a new atmosphere in Sarajevo. And as General Rose said to us, "Things were possible that weren't possible before. There was some prospect of reaching agreement to reduce shelling and sniping. The blue routes were opened. Civilians started to come back in," as did this 13-year-old boy and his sister utilising the blue routes. And so, on this date, the 22nd of July, 1994, he with his bicycle went window shopping at this point with his mother and sister. And as his mother and sister looked into a shoe shop, which is to the right of what we see here, he was shot in his stomach. And his family and some people nearby, some adults nearby, rushed him off to hospital, and he survived. Investigator discovered that in fact, there were two bullets. That about the time he was shot, which was to the right of a passageway that we see to the right of this photograph, second shot penetrated the awning over what was a coffee shop. Next image. There is the penetration of the awning. Next image. It then penetrated the glass behind it. Next image. And finally hit a wall at the back of the coffee shop. Next image. The investigators determined the source of the fire as being the ridge line indicated by the circle and the arrow, territory held by the SRK, with the benefit of lining up the holes. Next image. And here, we have a view clearly from the ridge, the area of the ridge, looking back. And this is what the shooter saw. We see the building with the shops at ground level. Next image. All right. The Defence in its submissions concluded this or said this: It cannot be concluded that this witness, that is, the victim, was the subject of intentional sniping. This conclusion is corroborated by the fact that there were there other kids nearby the witness, including his mother and sister, but there were no more shots or attempts of shooter to hit the other persons present at the site at the relevant time. The Prosecution says that is a desperate argument. The Prosecution case is that the objective of the shooter was achieved. Civilians had been shot. And quite clearly, as this family did, that having occurred, they dispersed quickly. They took cover. The Defence also suggested in its written submissions that the bullet was a ricochet from an exchange of fire, suggested in spite of the fact there was no evidence of any other firing. And when one pictures a scene, a cease-fire, families strolling around, children playing in the footpath, it is with the greatest of respect to the Defence, nonsense to suggest that that could happen at the same time as an exchange of fire going on between the two sides. Again, I think it's best put as a matter of common sense. When one pictures a situation, factors in a line of fire, this was a deliberate blast at civilians, including children, in a public street from the SRK side. Next image on the screen now is incident number 10. And at this point, perhaps I'll say a little bit more about the dispute with the confrontation lines. If we could go to the next image. Here we see the markings made by a Defence witness on the earlier map suggesting where the confrontation line really was, much further to the south. On this image, the area of Osrenska Street is marked by the Prosecution with the red circle. And so, this Defence witness had the red circle as being beyond SRK positions. First observation I'd make about this proposition by the Defence is that it is extraordinary that so many witnesses gave evidence that Osrenska Street was a notorious source of sniping fire, that none of them realised it was ABiH territory, that none of them realised that the SRK was on the other side of the hill, that they had nothing to fear from that flank of the ridge. That is what the Defence is suggesting. Next image. Mr. President, I would say we could go back into private session and we won't show any images. We will skip the next few images Excuse me, Mr. President. Mr. President, are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in private session, Mr. Ierace. You're waiting -- you want to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. That's my fault. Yes I did. Perhaps I can raise this in public session. I understand from Madam Registrar that the next three images are confidential exhibits, but that's not my recollection. The relevant witness gave evidence with a pseudonym but in open session. And I don't recollect his maps as being --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have the exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, that's P3728 -- I'm sorry, no, I correct myself. P3637. I think that's -- there's five maps in that bundle. And I had thought, given the status of his evidence, that they weren't confidential exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would his name appear on any of these exhibits while marking them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it was blanked out. There was a yellow sticker placed over the name. My recollection is that that was done at the time he gave his evidence so the maps could be viewed publicly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is showing that they are under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, that being the case, I do ask for private session for around a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In fact, less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness D gave evidence that he was a soldier for the SRK. He was called by the Prosecution. His primary position, he said, was in Grbavica alongside the river protecting four high-rise buildings from which snipers operated. He said, though, that up until May 1993, from June 1992, he spent five or six days on six or seven occasions at another position which was Osrenska Street. He marked the position on a map, and he said he was last posted there in February 1993. He was shown -- might I just clarify the colour photograph is also a confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have the exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3251 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Okay. He marked on a photograph taken from Osrenska Street the area of his positions, and from that photograph, one can see the city in the background. He said that again, his responsibility was to secure, to operate from trenches in front of a house from which snipers operated, a two-storey house. He could see the snipers' weaponry protruding from the house behind him. Very often, he heard the sound of firearms coming from the house. The snipers discussed the nature of their targets, which was "civilians and soldiers alike." He said that what they shot at was usually the intersections and the transversals as they were called, which were built horizontally around the city, broad roads down the width of the city, not longitudinally, and they formed intersections with the vertical roads. He said that with binoculars, his words, I could see some containers that had been set up to protect passersby who had to cross to the other side of the street, and there was sort of protection barrier from sniper fire or fire from this type of machine-gun or other weapons. And he identified machine-guns that were used from Osrenska Street. He was asked whether in spite of the existence of the barriers, the intersections were still targeted? And he said "yes, they were." He said, "if you looked through a pair of binoculars, you could always see somebody going up to the container or passing by behind the container on his way to a building. Sometimes people weren't as safety-conscious and would cross at points where there were no containers, and you could observe this clearly using your binoculars." There is powerful evidence that Osrenska Street, indeed, further north, that is, down the slope from Osrenska Street, was in SRK territory. He said that the intersections and containers were sniped and machine-gunned with the M84 type of weapon. He said there were tanks and an APC also stationed on Osrenska Street by the SRK. And he said that the firing was one way. The firing was from the SRK, not from the ABiH. And by that, I should clarify there was occasional sniping fire, but no large-scale initiatives from the ABiH side. Here, we see the relevant photograph for incident number 10 where a woman was crossing the road behind containers with her 8-year-old daughter. She has marked -- the mother has marked on the photograph the position of the containers. X marks the spot where she emerged from the cover of the containers; and as she did so, she was promptly shot. The bullet passed through her body and into the right hand and abdomen of her 8-year-old daughter. They were taken to hospital. In the background, we see the ridge on which Osrenska Street was located. Next image. Now, even though a witness for the Defence said Osrenska Street was on the other side, he nevertheless conceded that this view was available from SRK positions, it being the relevant area where the witness was shot, and her daughter. The Defence submissions in relation to this incident are that it is not possible that the woman and her child could have been targeted because they were hit almost as soon as they walked out from the containers. The Defence says "how is it possible for the sniper to have seen them, to have taken aim, for the bullet to have travelled a distance, and yet for them to be hit within a second or two of emerging from the container?" The explanation is, from the Prosecution and its submission is this, that may well be a powerful argument if it wasn't for the fact that we're talking about snipers who had been in place for at least nine months, twelve months at that stage. This incident happened on the 3rd of September, 1993. We have the evidence of Witness D that snipers were operating from Osrenska Street with professional weapons since June 1992. We have evidence, which I've already referred to, as to how in spite of containers, snipers worked how to get around that, how to wait, how to spot civilians when they emerged. So Mr. President, that is not an argument which, in the circumstances of Sarajevo in September 1993, holds much weight given the practices which had been developed. I'll move on to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you could find a suitable moment for a break within two or three minutes, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We now move to incident number 15. The gentleman on the screen drove a bulldozer. He was tasked by UNPROFOR to remove rubbish. With the breakdown of basic services in Sarajevo, rubbish built up and had to be removed. It was a health hazard. He operated his bulldozer to the right of this photograph where he was protected. But standing where he is, in the background, we see territory which he identified towards the top of the ridge as being held by the SRK. As he manoeuvred his bulldozer, he inadvertently backed into view, even though there was an UNPROFOR, appropriately painted, APC with him as he backed into that area, he received a blast of fire. Next image. This photograph marked by the witness, being a telephoto from the last position, clearly indicates the SRK position. We see the stadium to the bottom left. And behind it, the police academy. There was much evidence about the police academy, how the Bosnian Serb forces captured it earlier in the conflict, and how it became a known source of sniping fire. Next image. This is his bulldozer. The very one he was driving that day, although photographed in the last two years. No change made to its condition other than replacement of glass. Next image. He said that he was told by his workmen that over 60 rounds, they counted, going on the impact points, hit the cabin. The relevance of this is that the Defence suggests that the evidence does not make out that he was targeted. The Defence suggests that the evidence is to the effect that the bulldozer was targeted, not him. When one examines these photographs, one sees that the impact points are most closely placed in the vicinity of the cabin. Next photograph. Even closer, we see impact points around the door and on the rim where the glass was. The Defence suggests that there's no evidence that the glass was broken which supports their contention that he was not the target. There is no evidence that the glass was not broken. It was not put to him that the glass was not broken. The evidence is of impact points around the door which would have broken the glass. Next photograph. Is that a convenient time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. Ierace. We'll have a break and resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed. There seems to be something on your screen that causes you to smile.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's the absence of an operator, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The absence of an operator.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: She has gone missing. But I can proceed in her absence, I think. Firstly, two matters not of substance: I'm informed that at some stage in the last session, regarded at page 41, line 21, I referred to the Prosecution rather than the Defence. That was in the context of the suggestion that civilians should be moved from the city or from the front line area. Mr. President, secondly, at some stage during this next session, I will hand over to Mr. Chester Stamp who will address you in relation to the scheduled shelling incidents and the statistical evidence to an extent as well from the Prosecution and Defence. And then tomorrow morning, I will again at some stage finish off the submissions. Mr. President, before I return to our point on the confrontation lines, I note that we started in the area of the airport. We went through Dobrinja, Nedzarici, Alipasino Polje, Cengic Vila, and Hrasno, and shortly we will move into Grbavica. If we could have the next image on the screen, we see incident number 20. This incident involved a woman at home in an apartment in a block facing south, facing the SRK confrontation lines, waiting with her family for her husband who was an ABiH soldier to come home. It was after nightfall. The husband was a witness, and he said tellingly that he felt safer in the trenches on the front line than he did in the city. He was not the only witness to say that. And it was a powerful indicator of the risks that everyone faced away from the front lines. The point being that moving from front-line positions as was the case with Milida Halili's mother was no guarantee of safety at all. Nowhere in the city was safe from indiscriminate and deliberate fire against civilians. He returned home and was concerned that his family had not put up the blanket across the windows of the living area facing the front line. They had up some coverings, some plastic on one half of the window, but it was torn. He said something about the lack of the blanket. So they would have a coffee first, as his wife sat with her back to the windows, there was the sound -- a crashing sound, and then she said she was gone for, or words to that effect, and she died within minutes. It transpired that two bullets had entered the apartment, it seems, simultaneously. And the bullet one lower than the other, the one that impacted the window frame remained lodged in her body, it being the fatal bullet; the other continued further into the apartment, penetrated a wall between that room and a small hallway, went beyond that, through the door into the public area of the apartment. Could we have the next image, please. Now, on this map, we see again the front line of the SRK positions consistent with the front line being to the north of Osrenska Street marked by the victim's husband. So there is consistency with the Prosecution case. Next image. Here we see the view from the living area looking north, the ridge with Osrenska Street in the background in the distance. The victim was seated with her back to the windows. One can see that the windows were two halves that opened inwards. Yes, next one. The husband marked the portion of the ridge where he believed the fire came from. Next one. A close-up from the same position, of the ridge. Next one. Markings by the husband of the relevant part of the ridge that was controlled by SRK forces. We will skip the next image. Come back. Stop that. All right. The Prosecution case is that having regard, especially to the fact that there were two bullets, that is powerful evidence that again the window was targeted, the window emitting light. The Defence points out that the victim herself in all probability; the Prosecution agrees. This was indiscriminate fire. The source of light was a candle in front of the woman. One could only speculate as to whether there was a silhouette. The Prosecution does not invite the Trial Chamber to speculate. But what is clear, as the evidence by the concern of the husband, is that light was being emanated and that was enough. The fact that the two bullets were simultaneous suggests that there were two separate shooters firing at exactly the same moment. Again, strong evidence that the intended target, that is, the lit room, the room from which light was emanating, was the target. No evidence of any shooting before or after, an otherwise quiet night. Therefore, to suggest that the victim was accidentally killed in an exchange of fire has no evidentiary basis. The next image, we won't come to it just yet, concerns the evidence of Aernout Baron van Lynden, a war correspondent, a veteran of a number of wars, in the Middle East and elsewhere, who in his early years was a member of the military himself. A very impressive witness. This particular aspect of his evidence concerns his observations of a high-rise residential building coming under fire from SRK territory. We'll play the video first because of the commentary that was tendered into evidence, because he was a witness, speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That incident was not only witnessed by Baron van Lynden, but obviously clearly also by the fire chief Jusufovic, who was a witness. And he was shown some raw footage of the incident which included some extra at the end which was not in Baron van Lynden's clip, but which is sufficiently important to show again. Could we please have the next clip.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, there's no image on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. We've discovered the reason for that. Perhaps we can play it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, this is the -- we will shortly see the section which was not in the earlier footage. It begins now. We see individuals making their way down the face of a building. The fire chief explained that this was the same incident, and this was the side of the building facing away, that is, to the north, from SRK positions. Now, Baron van Lynden was questioned as to the basis of some of the things he said in the report. How did he know that the building was inhabited by civilians? He said that he interviewed them. He spoke to them to find out what use, not only what their status was, but what use had been made of the building, in particular, whether it had been used by the ABiH. And he made the comment: "Civilians in any war zone are always very wary of their property being used by the military in any way whatsoever because they are afraid that their opponents will then fire on that property, and the civilian population in Sarajevo was no different to anywhere else." How did he know that the fire came from the SRK side? Because he could see it, and as we saw on the video, they were incendiary rounds. There were no particular skill required to work out where the rounds were coming from. He said that he thought several hundred people lived in that block alone. The fire chief said it was the biggest apartment block in Sarajevo. There is no explanation, other than the obvious, as to why it was hit. It was terrorising the civilian population. He said that the firing continued into the building as the firemen attempted to put it out, something the fire chief told us happened time and again during the indictment period. He referred to the SRK protecting their fires. Moving on to the next image, the next video is a report by Carel Djederic from the BBC that came into evidence through Richard Gray. One of the reasons I want to show it is again it demonstrates especially at night one could see some rounds, at least some artillery rounds, and where they came from. We have a problem in playing that, so we'll move on. Mr. President, I'm experiencing problems with this presentation, so I think at that stage, I might stop for the day and hand over to Mr. Stamp, if it's convenient. And we'll sort out the problems with this particular presentation overnight. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that's the most efficient use of the time available to the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, then, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours, and good afternoon. I'd like to start by asking a question. Imagine if someone placed a mortar in your community, in a community within a city, and began to fire off rounds within 300 metres in that community. Would not every person living in that community know about it? Except for those who are comatose. It is submitted respectfully that in that type of circumstance, it would be expected that all the persons in the community would know that these mortars are firing therein. Mortars are heavy weapons, and it is not possible to conceal their firing in a city. Commandant Hamill said, and I'll quote him: "That the detection of mortars is actually quite easy because it has a very loud signature, that is, it makes a very loud noise when it is fired. Even at a low charge, charge 0, or charge 1, it is still a very, very loud weapon." The population of Sarajevo were subject to rigorous training over a very long period so that they would have fine-tuned their senses. They certainly, according to Hamill, would be able to hear the difference between the sound of a gun and a mortar after a while. I asked a question, and I refer to the passage from Commandant Hamill's testimony because it appears that the main thrust of the Defence in respect to the scheduled shelling incidents, particularly incidents 1, 2, and 3, is that the rounds that caused these many casualties were fired by elements on the Bosnian government side of the line. In their opening of the Defence, they used the expression "staged" in reference to the shelling incidents, and the Defence expert testified in respect of "these incidents," that the rounds were fired on very short ranges, and therefore, from within the confrontation lines. It seems, in fact, that this is the only real issue left in respect of these incidents. And the theory that they were fired by Bosnian elements against their own civilians, which is a sort of theory of self-inflicted mayhem is a theory of last resort. It is raised to counter overwhelming and convincing evidence that these several scheduled shelling incidents were clearly criminal acts. There is no evidence that at the relevant times of these incidents was there any military necessity, and military necessity, by that I mean in the context of international humanitarian law. There was no military necessity for firing into these areas. The human tragedies that resulted were from deliberate targeting of civilians or indiscriminate fire into these civilian areas. And these incidents were so notorious that the accused must have known about them or ought to have known about them. As a matter of fact, in respect to the first incident, there is evidence from Commandant, I think it is, Bergeron that he made a complaint at the accused headquarters at Lukavica to the accused's superior officers. And this is the very first incident, according to the witness, Butva, the SRK, that is, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, were monitoring the media on the Bosnian side. And the Prosecution in our closing brief has also summarised the evidence of specific protests made to the accused or to senior officers of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or the VRS command so that these events could not have escaped his notice. Much ado and questions have been asked by the Defence in particular of persons with some experience in artillery fire about technical possibilities. The casualties from the first three incidents resulted from 82-millimetre mortar rounds. Yes, they said, including Higgs. It is possible to fire the 82-millimetre mortar at relatively short ranges. However, mere technical possibility does not amount to reasonable doubt. If all the relevant evidence in respect to these incidents is taken into account, then practically speaking, one can conclude beyond a reasonable doubt that these incidents could not have been staged within these communities. As submitted in the Prosecution's closing brief, a very high degree of accuracy would have been required in order to stage any of these incidents using only one or two rounds. Although the Defence experts rather contradictorily suggested that the accuracy was very low in respect to mortars, the overwhelming evidence has been, and this is also the evidence of three Sarajevo-Romanija Corps mortar gunners that testified, that they were capable of a very degree of accuracy, indeed, they could hit within 50 metres of their target, within one or two shots. That level of accuracy for the incidents to be staged is consistent with the Prosecution's case. We submit that they were capable of accuracy. However, there are necessary preconditions before that level of accuracy can be achieved. A mortar that would have been engaged in such a mission of firing one or two shells into these civilian gatherings cannot simply be set up, shoot the one or two rounds, and then scoot. Firstly, the mortars would have had to be located in a static position with the barrel pointing in the proposed direction of fire over a projected period of time. The Bosnian side, therefore, who would have had mortars, a very scarce resource for them, pointing into their own territory. Next, these mortars would have had to fire off a few rounds in the direction that they intended to fire in order to suddenly, solidly embed the base plates into the ground and to record the fire for the purposes of later adjustment. And thereafter, they would have to remain in the same spot for the opportune moment to fire on the civilians. This, it is submitted, could not be accomplished unnoticed in any community. It could not have escaped the attention of the citizens of these communities, including many of them who testified at this trial. Are we to assume that these victim witnesses, many of whom were injured or lost loved ones, would sanction these self-inflicted atrocities by silence? On the map that was tendered through the witness Higgs, he reproduced the evidence of the direction of fire, as well as the evidence in respect to where the confrontation lines were. And an examination of the characteristics of the area between the scenes of the incident and the confrontation lines along the axis of fire can assist in clarifying this issue. There, it would also be helpful to analyse some of the photographs and videos that were tendered through many of the sniping witnesses who lived in the area along the line of fire for these three first incidents. Many of them were shown earlier by learned lead counsel. However, the first image I'd like to show is an enlargement of part of map 3644RH. Incident 1 is marked with a number 1 in blue. The distance between the confrontation line and the scene of the incident marked 1 is approximately 320 metres. Now, the distances between the crime scene and the confrontation lines have been estimated with varying degrees of accuracy by many civilian witnesses. However, the relevant distances need not be a matter of argument. In fact, they could have been agreed upon. The location of these incidents is not really a serious issue. And in this area, there is evidence from the ABiH 1st Corps Commander Karavelic of the location of the confrontation lines as well as evidence of the witness Hadzic, who was the brigade commander for Dobrinja. The red lines, the unbroken red lines, are the axis of the direction of fire for the two mortar rounds. And the broken red lines forming an outer cone shape allow for a 5 degree margin of error, which was allowed by Higgs. From the impact site, along the direction of fire, the line goes over the building that was on the eastern side of the parking lot where the incident occurred. Then it passes through a commuter square, then over a building, and finally into an open area in the vicinity of the confrontation lines where, within this cone in the direction of fire, could the offending mortar have been hidden from the citizens of this community or the soldiers who defended it at the lines. Some of the casualties in this incident were off-duty soldiers. Were they deliberately killed or injured by their comrades in arms? If so, what would have been the reaction of the survivors? It should also be recalled that these confrontation lines were normally defended by men who were from the very communities where the lines were located. They, too, had families and friends inside that attended the football tournament or that had to go out to fetch water or food for sustenance. Again, one could ask: What about the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps troops that were in the vicinity of these lines? Some areas within the cone of fire could be directly viewed from the SRK lines. Surely, they would have been able to observe the preparations and fire by the ABiH into their own territory. DP9 testified that his platoon was based in this area of the lines in Dobrinja; and although he spoke of trenches going up to Mojmilo hill, he did not mention anything about mortars in the area in this particular area, nor did he mention anything about mortars in this area firing back into the ABiH territory. Anyone who set up a mortar within this area would have been peppered by SRK counterfire long before they could even get a shot off. As regards the trenches which led up to Mojmilo, these trenches were actually trenches used by the civilians to cross from Mojmilo into Dobrinja, and vice versa. The evidence is that the trenches were dug for the civilians to protect themselves because of the constant sniper fire that was directed by the SRK forces from Lukavica area down that Lukavica main road. Witness R and Fata Spahic who were victims in the humanitarian line incident spoke about the purposes of these trenches. They, and other women, had used these trenches to travel to Dobrinja to try to get flour where the humanitarian aid was being distributed. They used the trenches to avoid sniping from the SRK forces in Lukavica. Along those trenches, they met only two soldiers that day. Hadzic, who ought to have known what were the circumstances in the area, testified that soldiers did have occasion to use these trenches. But when they did, they never fired from them. In regard to incident 2, and we need not move on, it's here. The configuration of the territory in the direction of fire leads to practically the same conclusion. There was no possibility of placing mortars within the cone of fire. And certainly, no possibility of not only placing mortars there, but to take the necessary preparatory steps of adjustment fire, and then firing on civilians within the lines. The impact site is marked 2, and the line of direction of fire is a solid or unbroken red line. In this incident, Higgs allowed a margin of error of 8 degrees on each side, possibly because in this incident the mortar rounded exploded on contact with a person at the gate to the water collection point. The distance between the impact and the confrontation line was approximately 250 metres. The map clearly shows that all the possible firing positions in the area controlled by the ABiH were visible from the lines held by the VRS forces or otherwise they were in the open, near to, and within view and earshot of the residents on the Bosnian side of the lines. Again, in such a case, it would have been impossible to position mortars and fire them without anybody registering it. It is submitted that the only reasonable conclusion is that the 82-millimetre mortar shell that fell among those gathered at the water collection point was fired from the area of Nedzarici as indicated by at least three witnesses who examined the area. And Nedzarici is well within the area controlled by the SRK. We'll see on the map below the number 2 a dot with a T below it. And that's in blue. The dot is the place or the location of a house where the trench to the tunnel which was built under the airport began. This is about 120 metres to the southeast of the scene of the incident. The evidence is, including documentary evidence tendered by the Defence, that this house came into use weeks after the incident of the 12th of July, 1993, and therefore, the house is not relevant to incident 2. Higgs had expressed the view, however, that the house would not have been the target as the error in the region of 120 metres would have been too great having regard to the angle of its position in relation to the direction of fire. And I'd like to comment briefly on that. One can see on the map that the dot representing the house is off to the right of the direction of fire. Higgs' reasoning is logical, because as has been explained by many witnesses, including Defence witnesses, there are many reference points, like buildings, intersections, and other landmarks that are used when firing artillery into a town. So with good maps, the gunners could very accurately point the barrel in the direction aimed at. In other words, the mortar tube can be aligned using the various reference points so that it points precisely in the direction of the target. The situation, of course, would be substantially different in the classic situation where the firing is done in open terrain. In the circumstances of this incident, it is highly improbable that a mortar battery firing from Nedzarici would make an error to such a degree to the right or left of the target. The same observations, it is respectfully submitted, would apply equally to the battalion headquarters which Hadzic had marked on his map which was tendered into evidence. That was located some 100 to 150 metres to the northwest of the incident point, or to the left of the direction of fire. If perhaps we could move on to the next one and the next one, this is the area of incident 3. The Chamber has already viewed photographs from witnesses in respect to the sniping incident who were shot somewhere in the vicinity of the school for the blind and along this line representing the direction of fire. The unbroken red lines start beside the number 3 where the incidents occurred, and go from the impact sites to the school for the blind. This is because during the conflict, the school for the blind had attained a remarkable degree of notoriety as the source of sniping, and many witnesses had heard shells, mortar rounds being fired from that area. It became a very well-known line to mark. According to Mirza Sablija -- may I pause here. I would respectfully ask that that be redacted, the name I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar will take the necessary steps. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am grateful, Mr. President, and I do apologise. I have been advised that --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is not a protected witness, Mr. Stamp. Facial distortion only.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that means that the necessary steps are no steps. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: According to Witness AI and Mirza Sablija, in the immediate vicinity of the Institute for the Blind, there were barracks of the former JNA. And these barracks were occupied by the SRK during the conflict. This is the area that Witness AI identified as a source of the sound of the firing of the round that injured him and the children. So the school building or the building of the school for the blind and that compound that the red line -- the red lines -- the unbroken red lines touch upon in the west are reference points as explained by Higgs. They are reference points for that area in Nedzarici. The 82-millimetre mortars that were fired were located on grounds in the general vicinity of the school and the military barracks, not necessarily in the schoolyard itself. Again, the map in conjunction with the various photographs that are in evidence clearly shows that positions of mortars and heavy weapons would have been visible from the lines held by the SRK forces or they would have had to be in small open areas, near to buildings that were occupied. There are major intersections, courtyards, and parking lots outside the apartment buildings in the Bosnian side of the line. The possibility of fire, it is submitted, from the Bosnian side of the line is excluded as a proposition which is mere technical possibility, but not a practical possibility. And in conjunction with the evidence of Witness AI, it is submitted that the certain conclusion is that these rounds were fired from Nedzarici. The last thing I'll say on this notion, this theory, that the Bosnian civilians were standing by and allowing certain elements to shoot and kill their own people is that self-preservation and protection of family and loved ones is a very basic human instinct. There is no reason to deny the Bosnian people of that basic human instinct. To even conceive and suggest that the residents of these communities and the soldiers that defended these communities quietly acquiesced in the murder and maiming of their own because they would have known about it is tantamount to denying them even this basic human instinct. And it is not surprising, therefore, that when many of these victim witnesses came to this Chamber and testified about their experiences, it was never suggested to them, they were never asked about mortars in their communities killing their friends and their families. Mehonic, Rasim Mehonic, was a man about the community. He was gravely injured. He lost his wife and two daughters in one incident in one day, he testified. He would have known about mortars firing on these people within a couple hundred metres of where he lived. In any community, any intelligent person would have known. He was not asked to comment on this possibility. According to Witness AI, who was also gravely injured, he was passing through phase B and heading towards phase C, Alipasino Polje, when he heard the first two shells that caused him to run for cover. He was injured in front of phase C. If one looks at the map, one can see that phase B is the two oval-shaped lines of buildings to the west of phase C where the incident occurred. That it is phase B is evident from the testimony of Witness Q. And I am going to pause shortly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You saw me looking at the clock, Mr. Stamp, I take it. Yes, yes, it's just in front of me. Yes, if you could find a suitable moment within one or two moments, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Phase B is a westernmost block of two oval-shaped apartments. This is where Witness AI was coming from. The Defence ballistic expert says that the two rounds that caused so many casualties, including AI, was fired from 200 metres away. 200 metres from these impacts in the established direction of fire can be measured on this map. And it puts the firing point within the courtyard of phase B, within the courtyard to -- in the set of buildings on the right. This is precisely where Witness AI was walking from. He would have been able to comment if he had been asked about the possibility that the mortars which killed these children and maimed him were located in the courtyard or the area that he had just walked from. May it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours, that is perhaps a convenient point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. Stamp. As far as I'm aware of, there would be approximately one hour and 15 minutes left if we stick within the five hours - I make the same mistake as I did this morning - the five hours granted to the Prosecution. That would mean if we resume tomorrow morning at 9.00, the Prosecution would be expected to finish at about 10.15. The Chamber will be very strict as far as time is concerned. We all know that part of the closing argument is also to some extent repetition, and acceptable repetition, of what has been written down in the final briefs. It's important to present this to the public who, of course, will not read all the documents that are filed by the parties. But at the same time, it indicates that it might be easier then while examining a witness to strictly keep within the time limits set. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.
